short: I’m a person from Media, PA who makes things across a bunch of different mediums. Photography, advertising, essays, software. Different tools, same person, mostly the same set of questions.
long:
Okay, the honest version.

I grew up inside a $60M evangelical church, which is a stranger sentence to write than it is to have lived. I studied theater in college, which sounds unrelated but really isn’t — a lot of what I do now is basically directing attention. Somewhere in there I picked up a camera and never really put it down.

Professionally, I’ve worked on things you’ve probably seen without knowing I was part of them. Campaigns for Hershey, Cadbury, Reese’s. Portraits for National Geographic. A stretch running the creative engine at UberFacts. I started a company called CLR Wear that’s trying to solve custom-fit clothing with software. I’ve done research at Johns Hopkins on how bias works — not to eliminate it, but to understand it as a kind of gravity you can steer with.

On the side (or maybe in the middle, hard to tell anymore) I make fine art photographs using slow processes like gum bichromate and analog color separation. I write essays on Substack about pragmatism and aesthetics and what it means to try to be a person on purpose. I read a lot of Dewey and Cornel West and think about juxtaposition a lot.

If there’s a thread through all of it, I think it’s this: I don’t really believe in the split between commerce and art, or between the sacred and the ordinary, or between rigor and warmth. The best work I’ve seen — and the work I try to make — treats those as false choices. A candy bar campaign can be genuinely tender. A darkroom print can be an argument. An essay can be a portrait.

I live in Media, Pennsylvania. I’m open to talking about pretty much anything — a project, a question, a plot twist. If you’ve read this far, thanks. That’s more attention than most bios deserve.
